WITH RECURSIVE target AS (
  SELECT s.symbol_id
  FROM code.symbols s
  WHERE s.file_id = 'auto_ontology/server/models.py' AND s.name = 'ApiModel' AND s.kind = 'class'
),
ancestors AS (
  SELECT cb.class_symbol_id AS class_symbol_id, 1 AS depth
  FROM code.class_bases cb
  JOIN target t ON cb.base_symbol_id = t.symbol_id
  UNION ALL
  SELECT cb.class_symbol_id, a.depth + 1
  FROM code.class_bases cb
  JOIN ancestors a ON cb.base_symbol_id = a.class_symbol_id
),
best AS (
  SELECT class_symbol_id, MIN(depth) AS depth
  FROM ancestors
  GROUP BY class_symbol_id
),
direct AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT cb.class_symbol_id
  FROM code.class_bases cb
  JOIN target t ON cb.base_symbol_id = t.symbol_id
)
SELECT b.class_symbol_id, b.depth
FROM best b
WHERE b.class_symbol_id NOT IN (SELECT class_symbol_id FROM direct)
ORDER BY b.depth, b.class_symbol_id

request:
Which classes inherit from ApiModel (auto_ontology/server/models.py) only indirectly, i.e. through at least one intermediate class of this repository, and do not name ApiModel directly in their class statement? An import alias of ApiModel (auto_ontology/server/responses.py imports it as _Payload) counts as naming ApiModel directly, and a subscripted base such as ListResponse[T] counts as its class. For each, give the class symbol ID and the length of the shortest inheritance chain to ApiModel (2 when the parent class directly subclasses ApiModel).

Requested output columns: class_symbol_id (string), depth (integer).
explanation: Finds the ApiModel class in auto_ontology/server/models.py and walks class_bases edges upward to compute the shortest inheritance depth for every descendant class. It then excludes classes whose class statement names ApiModel directly (base_symbol_id resolving to ApiModel), leaving only indirect inheritors with depth >= 2.
